Happy Thanksgiving Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock hunters, and welcome to showtime. We've been expecting Black Friday to bring with it a new wave of 40th Anniversary edition handhelds and accessories, and with the big day itself now in touching distance, it's time to get serious.
Here's what we know so far. Nintendo itself has publicly stated that it won't be restocking the Zelda Switch 2 until January 2027 - but that's not going to stop the retailers who have been stockpiling since launch. Walmart has already busted out the gate with a members-only drop at the top of the week in the US and Argos has had its own little party in the UK as well.
It's all eyes on Best Buy and Amazon, then, as both retailers have had ample time to re-fill their warehouses since their last bout of availability. Meanwhile, Smyths Toys has launched a suspicious new listing page for the handheld in the UK.
So where do we start? I'd recommend keeping the retailers listed below close to your chest. These stores have all dropped Zelda Switch 2 stock in the past but have been quiet over the last two weeks. Make sure you're signed in with payment and delivery information saved, and then check back regularly. We'll be right here, rounding up all the latest updates live as they happen.
I've been tracking hard-to-find stock for over six years now, starting with the incredibly limited releases of the PS5 and Xbox Series X. I've been reporting on how retailers operate with high-demand products, from anniversary releases to brand new consoles, ever since then - including the Nintendo Switch 2 itself.
Amazon was dropping new Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks every few days at the start of the handheld's life, though only in very limited numbers. It's been particularly quiet for the last week, though.
Pro Controller: Check stock
Ocarina of Time (digital): $54.99 (was $59.99)
Walmart removed its listing for the Legend of Zelda Switch 2 handheld a couple of weeks ago, but it's just appeared in time for Black Friday. That's certainly a suspicious move on the biggest shopping week of the year.
Pro controller: Check stock
Ocarina of Time: $59.99 $49.99
Target usually signposts its future drops, at least it did when the store ran new Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks timed with the release of Ocarina of Time. Right now we've got a simple 'out of stock' message, but keep a close eye for updates here.
Pro Controller: Check stock
Best Buy hasn't dropped any new Legend of Zelda Switch 2 handhelds since it ran its own midnight launch event for Ocarina of Time (with consoles up for grabs). Online, we're still 'sold out' here, though more inventory is on the cards.
Pro Controller: Check stock
Nintendo itself has announced that it won't be running Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks until January 2027, so it's likely out of the race this Black Friday.
Pro Controller: Check stock
GameStop is only running Legend of Zelda Nintendo Switch 2 restocks in stores, so you won't find any online stock here. The store looks like it's about to start running Pro Controller and carry case restocks online, though.
Pro Controller | Check stock
Amazon UK has been a pretty reliable source of Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks in the last few weeks, even if things have slowed down in recent days. Like its US counterpart, the site has been dropping a small number of special edition handhelds at a time. Watch out, though, there are price-inflated £499 models floating around here - this one should be £429.
Pro Controller | Check stock
Ocarina of Time | £59.99 £54.99
EE has had two Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks since launch day, but the boost here comes from those bundles. The site has previously been offering discounts on Ocarina of Time remake and Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream when bought with the device.
Smyths Toys has returned its Legend of Zelda Switch 2 listing this week, after removing the page entirely when it ran out of stock a while back. That's a fantastic sign for more drops to come over Black Friday.
Pro Controller | Check stock
Here's the thing with Very. It often bundles up difficult-to-find stock with extra accessories or games to keep resellers at bay. That means you'll be paying a little more here (though still only RRP for everything you're getting) but stock often holds out a lot longer.
Argos was previously offering Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock ahead of launch, but things look to have run dry now. The store organises its inventory by postcode, though, so it's always worth checking your local area's delivery and collection options.
Currys previously had a listing page up for the Legend of Zelda Switch 2, but it seems to have disappeared now, instead sending us to a generic consoles search page.
Nintendo has also stated more stock is on the way, so you'd expect its own store to be one of the first with fresh handhelds up for grabs.
It's not exactly concrete proof that we've got more coming our way, but Best Buy's note on its Zelda Switch 2 stock page is reassuring that more is on its way. Whether those handhelds hit the shelves in time for Black Friday is another matter, but they're certainly not gone for good.
We've got a busy day of scouring the web ahead of us, with Black Friday just around the corner and retailers expected to unleash all those lovely 40th Anniversary handhelds at the same time. Where are we today?
In the US, we're looking to Best Buy, Target, and Amazon for updates. None of these retailers have held Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks for some time now, so could have been stockpiling ahead of this weekend's festivities.
Meanwhile, in the UK The Game Collection's bumper bundle has now sold out - though stuck around on the shelves for a good few days. We'd recommend keeping an eye on Smyths Toys for more in the next few hours.
Walmart has dropped in the US and Argos has offered up more Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restocks in the UK so far this week, so it's all eyes on the rest of the retail world as we turn the corner to the Black Friday straight this week.
In the US, we're looking primarily to Best Buy for another chance at the handheld and potentially the Pro Controller as well. The store hasn't had any online restocks since launch day (though opened up for in-store orders in its midnight Ocarina of Time event). That's plenty of time to get the shelves ready for a Black Friday splash.
In the UK, I'd keep an eye on Smyths Toys and Amazon. The former was one of the first out the gate when stock first dropped, though removed its listing page from the site a couple of weeks ago. It mysteriously jumped back into action a few days ago, though, signaling movement behind the scenes. As for Amazon, it was dropping small amounts of stock fairly frequently for a little while before stopping. That could mean the site has been saving up for a Black Friday power move.
Even though it's tempting, I'd recommend avoiding resellers at the likes of eBay. Thanks to their hideoiusly inflated prices, you'll end up paying well over the odds for the console - and there's still a decent chance more units will emerge at stores before the week is out. It's still quiet Stateside for now, but that could change at any moment; restocks are expected for this week at some point, and if I had to guess, Best Buy, Amazon, and Target will be your best bet.
Argos has given us plenty of hope this week in the UK. The retailer launched a brand new Legend of Zelda Switch 2 restock yesterday afternoon, lasting more than an hour before running off the shelves. This was just for the handheld itself, with no sign of the Pro Controller or carry case.
Meanwhile The Game Collection has a proposition I'd only accept if you really need to lock in

articles.title_orig: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
articles.title_zh: Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
articles.content_orig:
A Rheinmetall facility in Kuwait was targeted by Iran, Italian and Kuwaiti authorities said
Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.
The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.
Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi saying "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by its military.
Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.
It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.
Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.
The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
Iranian-backed militias in the region have also carried out attacks on the US's Gulf allies.
Kuwait's Army said the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.
Meanwhile, Italy's foreign ministry said in a statement: "An explosion caused by a drone attack... occurred at a site where two Italian technicians from the company Rheinmetall Italia were working."
The two Italian nationals were working at an air defence detection station and performing maintenance work on systems used by the Kuwaiti Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa, citing Italy's foreign ministry.
Italian media outlets have named the two individuals. One of the men was reported to be 36, while the other was 65 and nearing retirement.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.
"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.
"Today's events are a further reminder that security in the Gulf is a security issue for us all."

articles.title_orig: Lawmakers Seek AI Oversight, Tighter China Chip Controls
articles.title_zh: Lawmakers Seek AI Oversight, Tighter China Chip Controls
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems.
Companies have put an unusually high volume of Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, on the market since new measures restricting Chinese companies renting access to advanced Nvidia chips were announced on Nov. 16, the people said.
Jack Duhamel, president of AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two people familiar with the matter told CNBC the surge in GPUs for sale was directly attributable to the new rule. Duhamel added that one company looking to sell Nvidia chips told GPU Mart the sale was related to the new rule.
The two people said it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload them because they were originally for use in data centers in which Chinese companies would rent access. They asked not to be named because they were discussing private information.
The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced an interim final rule as part of a clampdown on Chinese companies bypassing export controls, which effectively ban the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to China, by accessing them remotely in overseas data centers. The rule came into effect on Nov. 19.
Deals to find buyers for thousands of B300 GPUs, one of Nvidia's most advanced offerings, have been floated since the rule was announced, said Duhamel and one of the people.
Nvidia declined to comment. BIS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Nvidia has been facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips.
The chip giant warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action," sources previously told CNBC.
In July, the U.S. accused a Chinese AI lab, Moonshot AI , of accessing Nvidia chips via a facility in Thailand. CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that the company had sought access to the chips via data centers in Europe.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that the new rule announced last week was intended to close "loopholes."
"For a long time, we have not allowed the sale of Blackwell chips, which are the highest AI chips or similar chips to China directly," he said.
"Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries."
During Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, then-interim CEO Colette Kress said the company was still studying the controls, but expected performance to remain strong because demand for chips far exceeded supply.

articles.title_orig: Egypt detains a driver suspected of causing Cairo tanker crash that killed 31
articles.title_zh: Egypt detains a driver suspected of causing Cairo tanker crash that killed 31
articles.content_orig:
Footage captures deadly inferno along Cairo's Ring Road on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, that left 31 people dead, officials said. (Credit: AP/UGC)
Egyptian authorities said Thursday that a driver suspected of causing a fuel tanker crash in Cairo — sparking a massive inferno described by a witness as "God’s hellfire" and leaving 31 dead — has been taken into custody.
The deadly blaze erupted Wednesday during rush hour on a major highway surrounding the Egyptian capital, burning 27 vehicles and also leaving 26 injured. As of Thursday, traffic on the Ring Road returned to normal after most of the wreckage was cleared.
"It was God’s hellfire on the Ring Road," Salah Ahmed, a microbus driver who witnessed the inferno, told The Associated Press. "People are still in shock."
Another witness said to Reuters that victims were found trapped in their vehicles as "they did not have time to get out."
STATE DEPARTMENT PRESSES EGYPT TO RESPECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM AS CHRISTIAN CONVERT FACES POSSIBLE EXECUTION
Burned cars are seen as firefighters extinguish a fire involving a vehicle carrying fuel products on the Ring Road in Al-Warraq, Giza, near Cairo, Egypt, on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. (Mohammed Salah/AP)
Video footage taken near the scene showed a blaze completely engulfing the highway as people gathered to look at the flames.
Egyptian prosecutors said in a statement that authorities had detained the driver of a vehicle suspected of causing the fuel tanker to overturn, which resulted in the fire.
They said the driver told investigators he was speeding between lanes when he hit the oil tanker in the rear right. He then lost control of his car and veered far to the right while one of the fuel truck’s tires burst.
That caused the fuel tanker to hit the concrete wall of the highway and overturn, leading to the spill of fuel and the fire, according to the prosecutors' statement.
The stretch of the highway where the fuel tanker overturned is in Waraq, a densely populated neighborhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area.
PROTESTERS CALL FOR REGIME CHANGE IN IRAN FOLLOWING DEADLY CRASH THAT KILLED 13 OIL AND GAS WORKERS
A fire burns where a vehicle carrying fuel products overturned and caught fire on a major highway in Cairo, Egypt, on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. (Habiba Abd El Aziz/Reuters)
On Thursday, commuters and pedestrians stopped to examine the scene. Black scorch marks covered the metal railings of one of the highway exits, where pedestrians and hundreds of vehicles had been trapped Wednesday night.
A high-voltage electricity line also lay twisted on the ground amid the black soot, while piles of ash lined parts of the Ring Road, according to the AP.
For hours after the fire, the injured were still arriving at nearby hospitals as families gathered outside them in a mix of shock and grief. Authorities said 39 ambulances had been dispatched to the scene.
Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record, the AP reported.
Bystanders gather next to the wreckage of a fuel truck in the aftermath of a fire in the Al-Waraq neighborhood near Cairo, on Nov. 25, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a massive multi-car pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

articles.title_orig: Trump admin.: New tariffs on 14 countries, including China and Japan
articles.title_zh: Trump admin.: New tariffs on 14 countries, including China and Japan
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. is preparing new tariffs on 14 economies , including China, the EU, Japan and India, following investigations into what the Trump administration says are excess manufacturing practices that disadvantage U.S. commerce.
The administration launched those and other trade investigations in March , weeks after the Supreme Court unraveled a major piece of President Donald Trump 's tariff-heavy economic policy by striking down his "liberation day" duties. Trump has since been accused by critics of his tariffs of trying to revive the canceled duties using other legal authorities.
The latest action targets foreign economies that create, sustain or contribute to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors that the U.S. finds unreasonable and burdensome or restrictive to its commerce, a senior U.S. official told reporters Tuesday evening.
The new tariffs are "targeted," not blanket rates, and will vary for each economy, and many will not exceed the rates established in previously reached trade deals, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the forthcoming duties.
The rates, which mostly range from 15% to 20%, are "not really additive" and generally will not stack on top of existing duties, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" Wednesday morning.
"In effect, it'll look more like a top up," Greer said. "When it all nets out, it really will just top up a few percentage points."
An exception is China, which faces a 20% rate under the new tariff policy, "so it will go up some," Greer said. But at the same time, both countries are moving to remove tariffs on some of each other's goods in what Greer called "stability-generating activity through this action."
The senior U.S. official said Tuesday that the 20% rate will come on top of the so-called forced technology transfer-related tariffs of roughly 25%, which were implemented during Trump's first presidential term. U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods will therefore reach about 45%, give or take for different goods, the official said.
Average U.S. tariffs rates on Chinese goods stood at about 36.5% as of July, according to the Congressional Research Service .
Greer also said on CNBC that the new policy likely will not take effect for months.
"We've talked to our trading partners about this. They know what we're proposing," he said. "I think a lot of this is baked in, and I don't think any of these would actually take effect earlier than a couple months from now."
The administration says the tariffs target what it calls "overcapacity" — excess industrial production, often supported by government subsidies, that allows cheaper goods to flood global markets and undercut U.S. producers.
China has disputed the allegations. "The so-called 'overcapacity' does not really exist," China's foreign ministry said Wednesday before the official reports were released by the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, according to Reuters.
The overcapacity levies are being imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The Trump administration invoked the same statute to launch investigations into 60 economies over alleged forced-labor issues.
Those investigations, which also began in March, led to broad tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on goods from dozens of countries covering 99.4% of U.S. imports.
The Section 301 actions came weeks after the Supreme Court struck down the near-global tariffs that Trump had enacted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.
Shortly after the court's ruling, Trump invoked Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 to impose a 10% global tariff. That tariff expired after 150 days, and was immediately replaced with the forced-labor-related duties.
An ongoing lawsuit accuses the Trump administration of citing forced-labor issues as a "pretext" in pursuit of reviving Trump's worldwide tariff regime.

articles.title_orig: China opposes proposed US tariffs
articles.title_zh: China opposes proposed US tariffs
articles.content_orig:
Add Axios as your preferred source to
see more of our stories on Google.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and President Trump speak to reporters aboard Air Force One. Photo: Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP via Getty Images
The Trump administration proposed a new round of tariffs targeting China, the European Union and 12 other economies over policies it says have created excess industrial capacity.
Why it matters: Trump officials are pressing ahead with his trade agenda despite a Democratic midterm sweep fueled by affordability concerns.
Driving the news: The tariffs are the result of  a trade investigation that launched in March , The proposed tariffs are a narrower approach than the sweeping import levies the administration has previously imposed, a senior U.S. official said.
Between the lines: The administration proposed tariffs of up to 20% to 35% on other targeted economies, though lower rates apply to trading partners with deals in place.
The big picture: The investigation was conducted under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The administration contends that foreign industrial policies encourage companies to produce more goods than global demand can absorb, undercutting U.S. manufacturers.
What they're saying: In response to reports of the proposed tariffs , China dismissed U.S. claims of industrial overcapacity as a "false proposition" and urged Washington to preserve stable trade relations.
Of note: The U.S. is also proposing tougher trade measures against Brazil, after imposing 25% tariffs in July over alleged unfair trade practices amid tensions between Trump and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
The bottom line: Trump's tariff agenda is moving forward as Democrats in the incoming Congress look to curb presidential authority over trade policy and lower Americans' costs .

articles.title_zh: Humiliated Putin Gets Abandoned by His Evil BFF
articles.content_orig:
By clicking â SIGN UP â you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .
Russiaâs Vladimir Putin has been abandoned by one of the worldâs premier dictators amid a diplomatic loversâ tiff.
North Koreaâs Supreme Leader Kim Jong Un has furnished Moscow with its troops and munitions in the fight against Ukraine , with his soldiers clandestinely shipped west to the edge of Europe, where they fought inside Russiaâs borders to repel Kyivâs incursions and counterattacks.
Russia and North Korea's relationship has posed an uneasy proposition for the West.
But that backscratching has now ended, Ukrainian intelligence claims, after Pyongyang said it will cease military aid to Moscow.
It is also terminating deliveries of KN-23 ballistic missiles and artillery ammunition.
Kim walks by a memorial to North Korean troops killed in Russia.
Ukraineâs Main Directorate of Intelligence said Thursday that North Koreaâs feathers were ruffled by Moscow when it proposed de-escalation in tensions between North Korea and South Korea.
Ukraine said that the halt order was personally issued by Kim.
Could the bromance be in danger?
According to the Kyiv Post , the order came after Andrey Rudenko, the Russian Deputy Foreign Minister, said that his country planned to seek de-escalation on the Korean peninsula.
North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son-ui said Moscowâs request raised questions about alliances and relations with South Korea.
The two countries have a mutual agreement in place.
Alexander Kazakov/via REUTERS
The withdrawal of ammunition poses a substantial problem for Moscow. Ukrainian intelligence said that ammo from the isolationist dictatorship accounted for between 25 percent and 40 percent of those used by Russia, according to a Kyiv Post report from July.
According to the Post, there is no suggestion that the existing troops drafted in to help Russia are being pulled away. Rather, Moscowâs request for additional troops, bumping numbers from 8,500 to 50,000, is being stalled.
North Korea has sent thousands of troops to assist Russia.
In 2025, Pyongyang acknowledged its troops had been deployed to help repel Ukraineâs Kursk offensive.
North Korea has also banned Russian military aircraft from its airspace, in addition to munitions withdrawals.
The two leaders have long aligned on the world stage.
Sergey Bobylev/via REUTERS
South Korea is aligned with much of Europe and the West in its support for Ukraine and in its condemnation of Russia following its full-scale invasion in 2022.
However, South Koreaâs imports of Russian coal rose 35 percent in 2026 compared to last year, according to The Post.

articles.title_orig: Trump tells Putin to ‘pull back all military aggression’ as he tries for peace deal to end ‘complete bloodbath’ in Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Trump tells Putin to ‘pull back all military aggression’ as he tries for peace deal to end ‘complete bloodbath’ in Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
By ELINA SHIRAZI, US SENIOR POLITICAL REPORTER
Published: 12:26 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 26 November 2026
President Donald Trump has revealed he personally pressed Vladimir Putin to halt Russian provocations across Europe in an urgent push to end the Ukraine conflict, warning that the ongoing war has become 'a complete bloodbath.'
Taking to Truth Social on Thursday following late-night talks with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at Mar-a-Lago, the president disclosed what he told the Russian strongman during their recent face-to-face meetings in China .
The president said he urged Moscow to stand down 'in hopes that a deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly'.
The Truth Social posts followed a Wednesday night sit-down between Trump and Rutte at the President's Florida estate, which Trump dubbed 'the Southern White House '.
Trump reveals he 'spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe'.

articles.title_orig: Germany: 2 suspected Islamists arrested in Heidelberg and Cologne, suspected of plotting synagogue attack
articles.title_zh: Germany: 2 suspected Islamists arrested in Heidelberg and Cologne, suspected of plotting synagogue attack
articles.content_orig:
Germany 's federal prosecutor's office on Thursday said it had ordered the arrest of two Iraqi citizens in Germany who are believed to be members of a pro- Iranian terrorist group.
It identified the men as Mostafa Al-R. and Ameer J., and said that they were arrested in Heidelberg in Baden-Württemberg in the southwest, and in Cologne , several hours' drive to the north.
Officers from Germany's federal criminal police force carried out the arrests.
Prosecutors also announced searches and raids of 17 sites in total across three separate states, saying these were ongoing.
After two suspects were arrested, Hendrik Wüst, the premier of North Rhine-Westphalia , thanked the security agencies for their vigilance and dedication. "Protecting Jewish life is our shared responsibility," he wrote on X.
"Jewish life must be able to flourish freely and safely in our country. Anyone who attacks it attacks us all," Wüst added.
Prosecutors said the two men were "strongly suspected" of membership in a domestic terrorist organization.
They said that Mostafa Al-R. wa an associate of a man in the US known as Mohammad Al-Saadi, who is accused of setting up a group with the acronym HAYI (Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiyya) that is thought to be "responsible for a series of attacks against US, Israeli and Jewish institutions in Europe from March 2026," in the aftermath of the outbreak of Donald Trump's war with Iran .
Mostafa Al-R. and Al-Saadi allegedly "founded a separate organization to prepare and carry out further attacks in Germany and Europe at the end of 2025."
Prosecutors say Ameer J. joined this group. It gathered funds and "recruited several external people to carry out explosive attacks."
"On the group's orders, unknown assailants headed on two consecutive nights in late March 2026 — presumably with explosives — to synagogues in Cologne and in one other European city," prosecutors wrote. "The plan was, for reasons as yet unknown, ultimately not carried out."
Prosecutors said that intelligence behind the arrests could be traced back to the federal domestic intelligence agency , the BfV.
More than 250 police officers from various forces were part of Thursday's operation.
Both suspects were expected to appear before judges later on Thursday for a decision on them being placed in investigative detention.
One other person is being sought as part of the investigation, with several others not currently suspected of criminal offenses affected by it.
The stated date for the plot to attack Cologne's synagogue, late March this year, would have roughly coincided with a series of crimes in Europe targeting Jewish people or institutions in the weeks after the outbreak of war with Iran.
These included an explosion in front of Liege synagogue in Belgium on March 9 , which caused property damage but no injuries.
Police in the Netherlands investigated a fire at Rotterdam's synagogue a few days later . An explosive device was set off outside a Jewish school in Amsterdam soon after , prompting heightened security across the Netherlands.
In London, a Jewish ambulance service was targeted in arson attacks in March , not long before two Jewish men were stabbed in broad daylight in what investigators treated as a likely act of terrorism.
Several months later, in September, police in Wuppertal in Germany arrested an Afghan national on suspicion of trying to set a fire at the city's synagogue.

articles.title_orig: Trump’s Latest Tariffs Revive Focus on Pressuring China
articles.title_zh: Trump’s Latest Tariffs Revive Focus on Pressuring China
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks on reciprocal tariffs during an event at the White House on April 2, 2025.
China warned Thursday that it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to retaliate against the Trump Administration’s proposed new tariffs , which have reignited global trade tensions.
“China urges the U.S. to correct its wrong practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” said He Yadong, spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce. He added that Beijing “reserves the right to take necessary measures and will resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.”
The Trump Administration targeted 14 trading partners Wednesday in a slew of new tariffs that are set to come into effect early next year. The levies will be imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 following an investigation led by U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. The U.S. said the probe had found demonstrations of unfair trade practices and excess manufacturing capacity. Mexico and Norway were not listed in the new proposals, as investigations into their respective trade practices are ongoing. Greer framed the tariffs as a way to “level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy.” The Section 301 avenue is a way for the Trump Administration to reinstate many of the tariffs that were deemed illegal and struck down by the Supreme Court in February.
China is facing a 20% tariff, which the Trump Administration said it could double to 40% if Beijing does not adhere to the terms of an existing trade truce with Washington.
Another major U.S. trading partner, Vietnam, is facing tariffs of up to 35%. The country’s Ministry of Industry and Trade said it was in the process of “developing and submitting counter-arguments to the preliminary conclusions and inaccurate opinions and allegations from relevant parties.”
Agathe Demarais, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, views the tariff proposals as a pressure point on Southeast Asian economies and their trade relations with the U.S. and China.
She says that many of the region’s economies see a lot of Chinese goods pass through before heading to the U.S. market, with tariffs intended to “make it more difficult for economies like Vietnam to position themselves as collector economies between the U.S. and China,” she tells TIME.
The proposed tariffs are subject to a public notice and comment period, with a hearing set to take place early next year before they go into effect, allowing countries to issue responses and arguments.
Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Singapore-based Hinrich Foundation, says the proposed measures are already generating significant “resentment” among trading partners.
On top of that, the proposed rates have prompted uncertainty for major economies as to what Washington could do next. “If the U.S. unilaterally determines that the partner is not living up to expectations, then the number can ramp up higher,” she says. “That doesn't really support trust, and it makes it very hard to plan ahead.”
Amid rising tensions, several trading partners are already following China’s lead in voicing their disapproval over the rates.
Bernd Lange, trade committee chair in the European Parliament, said it was “absurd” the E.U. is facing a 20% tariff. He expressed hope that any enforced tariffs will adhere to the Turnberry agreement signed between Washington and the E.U. last year, which capped U.S. tariffs at 15%.
“Washington’s allegations about E.U. industrial overcapacity are absurd. We’ll now see whether the announced U.S. tariffs comply with Turnberry in practice,” he said. “If Washington breaches its commitments, the E.U. must act swiftly. It has the legal means to do so.”
Elms says the threat to hike rates against economies that already have a trade pact with the U.S. further calls into question “how durable” trade commitments with Washington are.
Overall, the proposed rates are just “one more complication in the relationship with the U.S.” that global partners have to contend with, adds Demarais.
Singapore and Japan also hit back at the prospect of respective 20% tariff rates.
Singapore’s Ministry of Energy, Trade, and Industry said it was “very disappointed” by the assessment and argued that the U.S. Trade Representative’s findings “do not take into account the structure of Singapore’s economy.” Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara referred to the U.S. tariffs as “regrettable,” insisting that: “Japan does not have any nonmarket policies or practices, or structural excess production capacity in the first place.”
Alongside the sweeping tariffs against 14 trading partners, the Trump Administration published a separate proposal seeking to raise levies on Brazil by specifically targeting its sugar and aircraft exports.
“Imposing an additional, specific tariff on sugar imports from Brazil and an additional 10% tariff on finished aircraft exports from Brazil is intended to help bring Brazil to the table,” said the office of the USTR (U.S. Trade Representative). The announcement came amid stalled trade talks between Washington and Brazil.
The Brazilian government expressed “outrage” over the proposed raising of rates, arguing that it has “been acting in good faith in negotiations” relating to Section 301 with the U.S. for over a year.
“The USTR's unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the ongoing bilateral negotiation process. Brazil will not yield to this type of threat,” the government vowed in a statement.
It said Brazil would continue to negotiate with the U.S., “without ruling out the possibility of adopting retaliatory measures in response to the illegal and unjust imposition of tariffs on Brazilian products.”
The Trump Administration could face significant pushback from the U.S. Congress next year, as Democrats will take control of both the House and Senate in January following sweeping victories in the midterms.
Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon, who will chair the Senate Finance Committee next year, has vowed to try and overturn Trump’s tariffs.
“This is another blatant attempt by Donald Trump to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs, no matter the cost to American families, workers, and small businesses. Global overcapacity is a serious problem, but Trump’s unilateral price-hiking tariffs are not the solution,” Wyden said in a statement . “As incoming Finance Committee Chairman, I will use every tool at my disposal to end Trump’s tariff chaos and restore Congress’ constitutional authority over trade.”
However, securing a veto-proof majority to rein in Trump’s authority could well prove difficult.
Among the general public, tariffs remain deeply unpopular with Americans. An NBC News exit poll following the midterm elections found that 66% of voters believed Trump’s tariff policies had hurt the national economy.

articles.title_orig: Trump calls the pre-election GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of Commerce Department
articles.title_zh: Trump calls the pre-election GDP figures 'fake' and demands an investigation of Commerce Department
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump on Thursday falsely deemed the latest gross domestic product revision a mistake, claiming that it should be "immediately investigated."
Data released Wednesday from the Commerce Department revealed that the U.S. economy exhibited much stronger growth for the third quarter than initially estimated, showing that real GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized rate . That was revised upward from the department's advance estimate of 3.4%.
That revision was a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," Trump said in a Truth Social post , suggesting that the initial release could have influenced the outcome of the 2026 U.S. midterm elections , where Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress and even multiple governorships.
"I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated," Trump wrote.
However, the difference between the advance estimate and the figure in the second release is far from being an all-time record. It was the largest revision since the 1.2 percentage point revision seen in the second quarter of 2020.
On an absolute basis, the latest revision was tied for 16th among all revisions from the advance estimate to the second release since 1990. It also tied four other quarters with a similar 0.9 percentage point difference — and was approximately double the average revision of 0.43 percentage points for all 147 quarters.
CNBC has reached out to the White House for comment.
Revisions to U.S. economic numbers are not necessarily out of the ordinary . Initial reports count on partial survey data and early estimates. Those data are later updated with more survey responses — which sometimes leads to changes from the initial reports.
GDP data is revised repeatedly over a five year period. By the time the final revision is done, the average absolute error from the second release to the final is 1.14 percentage points.
Notably, the advance estimate for Q3 U.S. GDP, which came just days before Election Day in early November, was still better than the figure economists had expected at the time. It also showed a significant step-up in growth from the second quarter.
Because that was a strong showing for the economy, some on Wall Street consider this week's revision to be confirmation of the economy's recent growth trend.
Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors said immediately following the release that it "reinforces an increasingly familiar tension" that the economy is "performing quite well, but its resilience also gives the Fed an even stronger case for further rate hikes."
"The economy isn't merely hanging in there. It continues to demonstrate considerable resilience, with consumers spending, businesses investing and few signs that restrictive monetary policy is creating significant cracks in the broader expansion," the firm's chief investment officer said.
Traders are currently pricing in a nearly 100% chance of a hike at the Federal Open Market Committee's December meeting, per the CME FedWatch tool . They're also anticipating an additional hike in January.
— CNBC's Jeff Cox and Fred Imbert contributed reporting

articles.title_zh: Trump Says He Asked Putin to End Russia’s Military Aggression Across Europe During China Talks
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
US President Donald Trump says he has told Russian leader Vladimir Putin to “pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe ” in the hope this could lead to a quick settlement of the war in Ukraine.
“During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia , I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly,” Mr Trump wrote in a Truth Social Post.
“I really believe this is a strong possibility – Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH.”
The US president has frequently urged a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine.
On Thursday, however, he used broader language about “territories throughout Europe”, without specifying what that meant.
Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine started in 2022, other countries occasionally have accused Russia of provocative behavior.
Poland, a Nato member, this week accused Russia of deliberately violating Polish airspace.
Estonia recently linked an arson attack to Russia's military intelligence service.
Mr Trump made headlines when he warmly greeted Russian leader Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during the Apec summit in China.
The commander-in-chief's enthusiastic reception of Mr Putin was condemned by commentators and former diplomats who labelled it an embarrassment for America.
Former US ambassador to Russia Michael McFaul said that his decision to call Mr Putin his “friend” was radically out of step with American society.
Back at the White House, Mr Trump was asked whether Mr Putin was also a friend to the United States.
“I can't speak to America,” he replied, while emphasising his “very good” personal relationship with the Russian leader.
He later posted an image of himself standing close to Mr Putin and shaking his hand beneath a caption in large type: “My Friend.”
It was one of dozens of photos he shared from the summit throughout the course of the day, many of which depicted him alongside the Russian leader and Chinese President Xi Jinping .

articles.title_orig: Musk makes $18 billion SpaceX stock pledge for every kid in America
articles.title_zh: Musk makes $18 billion SpaceX stock pledge for every kid in America
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX said Wednesday it will donate one share of the company's class A stock to every active Trump Account , and CEO Elon Musk would personally match the gift.
"SpaceX is building the infrastructure of the future and working to make life multiplanetary," the company said in a statement. "We believe ownership of the company creating these systems should extend to the next generation of Americans for their long-term benefit."
The White House announced in October that nearly 70 million Trump Accounts had been created, including more than 60 million through auto-enrollment. It's unclear how many are considered active.
Musk said in a social media post on X on Thursday that the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, without providing further details. "The share directly from me will be transferred when my lockup expires in June next year," he added.
Eligible children must have their account claimed to enable contributions from family members, friends and employers, and to receive the government's one-time $1,000 seed contribution. Auto-enrolled children can receive philanthropic contributions without a parent or guardian claiming an account, according to TrumpAccounts.gov.
Representatives for SpaceX and the U.S. Department of the Treasury did not immediately respond to a request for further details about the planned gift.
SpaceX Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell had previously agreed to make a personal gift of over 2 million SpaceX shares to Trump Accounts, with eligible account holders expected to receive them in December .
In October, Elon Musk posted on X that he would give a share of SpaceX to every kid in America next year.
Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts, are open to any U.S. child under 18 with a Social Security number.
Parents, guardians, grandparents and others can collectively contribute up to $5,000 per child per year in after-tax dollars up until the year before the beneficiary turns 18. The annual contribution limit is indexed for inflation after 2027.
Since the July 4 launch, families and friends have collectively contributed more than $1 billion to Trump Accounts . Total deposits now sit at more than $9 billion, CNBC first reported.
Children born from 2025 through 2028 may receive a one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury. Other funds may also be available, depending on certain criteria.
The Treasury rolled out temporary regulations at the end of September that allow Trump Accounts to hold stock donations , a move officials have said is meant to encourage more philanthropic gifts.
Contributing stock can benefit donors, who are able to avoid capital gains taxes triggered by selling appreciated stock. But families can face restrictions related to selling that donated stock. The policy also means some children's wealth accumulation could be tied to the performance of individual companies.
Under U.S. Department of the Treasury guidelines, families cannot refuse stock gifted to Trump Accounts and generally cannot sell it until the earlier of five years or the end of the calendar year in which the beneficiary turns 17.
SpaceX shares have been under some pricing pressure as the company negotiates a possible merger with Elon Musk's automaker Tesla . The companies have established two special committees to handle merger negotiations, and hired advisers for a potential mega-deal.
CNBC's Sam Meredith, Kevin Breuninger, Kate Dore and Jess Dickler contributed to this story

articles.title_orig: FedEx Cargo Jet Skids Off Miami Runway
articles.title_zh: FedEx Cargo Jet Skids Off Miami Runway
articles.content_orig:
MIAMI INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT, FLA. (WSVN) - A cargo plane skidded off a runway at Miami International Airport, Wednesday night.
7News cameras captured emergency crews surrounding the FedEx cargo plane that skidded off one of the airport’s runways after overshooting the landing.
As of Thursday morning, the FedEx plane is still sitting in the same spot it landed in.
The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed the McDonnell Douglas MD-11 originally departed from Frederick W. Smith International Airport in Memphis before coming to MIA.
According to an MIA spokesperson, the aircraft overran Runway 26R at around 8:30 p.m., stopping just short of a fence along Northwest 67th Avenue.
Officials said Miami-Dade Fire Rescue crews responded within 15 minutes.
“Attention all units, attention all units. We have an aircraft that just went off the runway,” an official is heard saying through Broadcastify.
Officials said no injuries were reported, and both people that were inside the cargo plane were seen disembarking and being met by emergency crews.
This outcome was much different from the Sept. 6 incident, in which a 21 Air cargo plane flying for Amazon Prime overshot the runway, crashed down and killed five airport employees while injuring five others.
On Nov. 14, two aircrafts collided on the taxiway at MIA, leaving both planes damaged.
Audio from the control tower on Wednesday’s incident captured the moment officials announced an initial 45-minute ground stop after the FedEx plane ran off the runway.
“The airport is closed. You can cross the runway, cross the runway,” an official is heard saying through Broadcastify.
The closure triggered hourlong delays to departing flights across the board.
On Wednesday night, over 560 flights were delayed and 64 were canceled.
Three out of four runways are operating as of Thursday morning, with FlightAware reporting 138 delayed flights and 35 canceled flights.
“It’s kind of terrifying, it’s kind of scary, and I’m just like, ‘What’s happening?’ You know, it’s just really unfortunate when it’s around the holidays that, you know, we’re going to miss this time with our family and stuff,” said a traveler.
Greg Smith told 7News he was trying to get back to London when he found out about the delay.
“We came in, everything was on time for a 10 o’clock departure, we had a little bit to eat, then that’s when we found out everything got diverted to Orlando,” said Smith.
FedEx released a statement Wednesday night, saying:
“FedEx Flight 910 from Memphis to Miami experienced an issue upon landing Wednesday evening at Miami International Airport. We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries. We are coordinating closely with investigating authorities, and any additional questions should be referred to the FAA.”
MIA officials advise travelers with flights scheduled for Thursday to check in with their airlines for the latest updates on the status of their flights before making their way to the airport, with delays and cancellations expected to continue throughout the day.
The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board are investigating what led to this incident.

articles.title_orig: How the Black Sea front in the Russia-Ukraine war is threatening to pull the U.S. into the conflict
articles.title_zh: How the Black Sea front in the Russia-Ukraine war is threatening to pull the U.S. into the conflict
articles.content_orig:
Constanța, Romania – Out on the Black Sea, the Romanian Navy is always on the lookout for the deadly debris of a war it isn't fighting.
It's a front of the Russia-Ukraine war that most people rarely see. It runs right up to NATO's doorstep and sometimes crosses into its waters — threatening to pull the alliance, and therefore the United States, into the war.
Incidents involving drones, mines and commercial ships are surging in the Black Sea, NATO military spokesperson Colonel Martin O'Donnell told CBS News.
"In 2025, for example, we saw fewer than 50 incidents in the Black Sea. This year alone, we're talking four to five hundred," he said.
The roughly tenfold increase threatens a major artery of global grain and fuel shipments and has made the waterway deadlier than the Strait of Hormuz , a flashpoint in the U.S.-Iran war, with both sides trying to enforce blockades on the chokepoint to exert economic pressure on the other.
Twenty-five sailors have been killed in the strait this year, according to the International Maritime Organization , while at least 40 have been killed in the Black Sea in the same period, according to the International Transport Workers' Federation .
"I would say the Black Sea is just as important, and then depending on who you talk to, some might argue could perhaps even be more important … in terms of global trade," said O'Donnell.
Any imbalance in the flow of fuel and food "can have global implications that can impact America just as much as it can any of the nations here," he said.
And this maritime front stretches beyond the Black Sea.
Over the weekend, Ukraine said it struck an advanced Russian warship and a cargo ship that then drifted, on fire, into the waters of NATO member Finland.
On Sunday, Ukraine said it sank a Russian warship docked in Libya.
Three of the six countries bordering the Black Sea are NATO members — Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey.
But as Romanian Navy Captain Mihai Iordache explains, defending those borders is nothing like defending them on land.
"We do not have a fence into the Black Sea to state this is our border, that is the other border," he said.
The Romanian Navy is deploying highly specialized divers and drones, scouring the depths for unexploded weapons.
All this comes as the pressure on NATO is mounting. On Friday, Poland accused Russia of "intentional provocation" as Russian cruise missiles landed in the country's southeast.
Drones have repeatedly entered the airspace of Poland and other NATO countries, mostly near Ukraine but not all, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022.
The Article 5 collective defense clause in NATO's founding charter states that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all 32.
Asked whether the alliance will defend itself if necessary, O'Donnell told CBS News: "I would say that there should be no doubt on NATO's willingness and ability to act."
On the Black Sea, Captain Iordache warns the Romanian Navy is already stretched thin.
"We don't have enough people, personnel, equipment to deal with all the commercial ships and all the drones that we have," he told CBS News during an embed.
"Four years ago, we were ready for one drifting mine, and right now we are ready for tens of drifting drones," he said. "So I presume we'll be ready in the future, who knows what the future will bring."
"Could be hotter, could be colder, who knows. Let's hope for peace."

articles.title_orig: Stocks rally, Europe sizes up next ECB chief
articles.title_zh: Stocks rally, Europe sizes up next ECB chief
articles.content_orig:
Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank next year.
He received backing from euro zone leaders at the European Council Summit, multiple media reported on Thursday.
The role still requires formal appointment after consultation with the European Parliament and the ECB's Governing Council, but neither has veto power and the decision follows intense political wrangling to reach a consensus on who should serve the eight-year term.
Reuters reported that de Cos was set for the nomination after the Netherlands agreed to back Klaas Knot, the only other candidate, citing European diplomatic sources.
De Cos is a 55-year-old economist and career central banker who rose through the ranks of the Bank of Spain, starting as a researcher in the 1990s and working in various departments before becoming governor from 2018 to June 2024.
He chaired the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision from 2019 to 2024, and has been General Manager of the Basel-based Bank for International Settlements since July 2025.
Both de Cos and his main rival for the ECB top job, Knot, were widely seen as candidates with deep knowledge and experience in monetary policy and financial stability — attributes that took on particular importance at a time of resurgent inflation, fragmentation and political uncertainty.
Lagarde had extensive experience in financial institutions but was criticized by some early in her tenure for a lack of central banking experience.
De Cos gained sufficient political backing in closed-door discussions and negotiations since Lagarde said she would step down on Feb. 7, 2027, over seven years after she became the first woman to helm the ECB. That was despite a final push by the Netherlands at the European Council meeting this week backing Knot.
Representatives from the euro area's biggest economies — Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands — have been horse-trading as they look to secure representation on the central bank's six-member Executive Board.
Influential roles as chief economist, expected to go to Germany's Markus Brunnermeier, and head of the Markets Portfolio, for which France's Laurence Boone has reportedly been tapped, also change hands in 2027.
Analysts say de Cos's commentary and actions over more than two decades at Spain's central bank paint him as moderately dovish — inclined to favor lower interest rates to support economic growth — but also as a pragmatist who has been willing to adapt.
That has included support for strong rate hikes during the energy price shock that followed Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, but also giving staunch backing for rates below zero and the huge stimulus package launched by then-ECB President Mario Draghi to reboot the euro zone economy in 2019.
De Cos quipped in 2024 that he was an "owl" after being asked if he was a hawk or a dove, emphasizing his focus on data and the situation at hand.
"It is true that Hernández de Cos supported the ECB's uber-dovish monetary policy during the period when inflation was persistently below target. However, his monetary policy views may well be regime-dependent," Christian Kopf, head of fixed income and foreign exchange at Union Investment, said in emailed comments.
"We are now clearly in a higher-inflation regime, with core inflation in the euro area expected to remain above the ECB's target through 2029."
Kopf added that de Cos was the candidate with the "strongest technical understanding of monetary policy and central banking," which he said was important at a time when the world is "witnessing an assault on central bank independence, not only in the United States but also in countries such as Japan."
"By appointing a career technocrat such as Hernández de Cos as ECB President, the European Council would send a strong signal that Europe will not waver in its commitment to price stability and that the euro will remain a hard currency," Kopf said.
Spain's de Cos as president, Germany's Brunnermeier as chief economist and France's Boone as head of market operations represent a "carefully crafted package deal," Kopf also noted, because it balances representation from northern and southern European countries. The result was partially due to the knock-on effects of the German government pushing hard for the chief economist position, he said.
Along with a desire among politicians for influence, a north-south balance is seen as important as the northern countries are seen as leaning more hawkish — more inclined to opt for rate hikes and restrictive policy to tame inflation — while southern are perceived as more dovish.
John Orchard, chairman of the Digital Monetary Institute at think tank OMFIF, said that as a "central banker's central banker," de Cos had "managed to earn respect from typically hawkish northern observers."
Another supportive factor of de Cos's candidacy was the stellar growth rate of many of those southern economies in recent years.
Once the "sick men" of the euro area's 2010s sovereign debt crisis, Portugal, Italy , Spain and Greece have become some of the bloc's strongest growth drivers in recent years .
Factors such as strong tourism, relative political stability, increased foreign investment and strengthening public finances have boosted southern economies. Meanwhile, the euro zone's traditional powerhouse Germany has stuttered amid soaring industrial costs and a struggling autos market .
Orchard said that some believed that Lagarde's presidency had ushered in an "esprit de corps" at the ECB, with policymakers focused on the interests of the whole European economy.
That would, in theory, reduce the importance of nationality among leadership and of traditional notions of hawkish northern nations and dovish southern ones. However, Orchard also noted the recurrent theme of national representation in the recent debate and the perception of Knot as a hawkish choice.
Diverging performance is a core challenge for any leader of the ECB, which must set monetary policy for 21 economies all growing at different speeds and with their own domestic priorities and inflationary pressures.
But it has become particularly pressing this year as the bloc's second-biggest economy, France, is teetering on the edge of its own potential debt crisis .
Moves in French markets and whether the ECB needs to take more extreme measures beyond continuing to urge fiscal discipline will remain in focus for de Cos.
The ECB Executive Board's view of what measures could be taken to prevent market disorder and under what conditions was a key topic under discussion when choosing who should fill the roles, according to insiders.
Despite political efforts to pass a budget that will reduce its budget deficit to around 5% of GDP, investors have been driving up French borrowing costs on concerns over its mounting public debt-to-GDP ratio , high budget deficit and contracting economy .
Risks are being compounded by political uncertainty ahead of France's presidential election in April, which is stymying business activity and raising wider questions about EU unity as far-right and far-left candidates pull ahead.
Rising French yields and the widening spread in France's borrowing costs over Germany's have led to speculation over whether the ECB might need to deploy tools such as liquidity injections or its never-used Transmission Protection Instrument to protect other countries from contagion and support the euro.
This would be politically controversial unless France agreed to stringent fiscal discipline measures akin to those that southern nations signed up to during the Sovereign Debt Crisis — which could be complicated if far-right presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, who has a combative relationship with EU institutions, wins.

articles.title_orig: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
articles.title_zh: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
articles.content_orig:
Israel has intensified its campaign of targeted assassinations in Gaza, striking and killing Hamas commanders and political leaders, as the Trump administration urges Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to proceed with the US-brokered ceasefire plan.
On Thursday, the Israeli military killed Khaled Abu Nada, a senior member of Hamas’ Political Bureau and the organization’s Deputy Minister of Education, in a strike in central Gaza. According to a statement from Hamas, the strike on his residential apartment also killed his wife.
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said the killing of Abu Nada would disrupt Hamas’ “financial operations and its ability to formulate economic policy.” Hamas said the attack was the result of Israel’s “policy of systematic assassinations” and warned that “targeting civilian homes constitutes a continuous breach of the ceasefire agreement in Gaza and a flagrant violation of all international and humanitarian laws, norms, and conventions.”
Israeli bombardment has left Gaza a ‘toxic wasteland’ for decades to come, report says
Since the nominal ceasefire was signed more than a year ago, Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza to target Hamas. According to the Palestinian Ministry of Health, more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza in Israeli strikes or military operations over that period.
In recent weeks, Israel has escalated those strikes. On Wednesday, Israel struck and killed Muhammad Abu al-Aouf, the head of Hamas’ internal security apparatus in northern Gaza. A day earlier, the IDF killed al-Aouf’s commander, Naeem Muhammad Abu Nahal, who led Hamas’ internal security across Gaza. In each of these cases, the IDF said the assassination was a “blow” to Hamas’ leadership capabilities, even as the militant organization has firmly entrenched its power in the half of Gaza not occupied by the Israeli military.
The previous week, the IDF carried out strikes nearly every day targeting Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad, from platoon leaders to commanders of Nukhba, a special force within Hamas’ military wing.
In each case, the IDF issued virtually the same justification: “Throughout the war, and particularly recently, the terrorists advanced attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians and operated to restore the capabilities of terrorist organizations in the Gaza Strip, in systematic violation of the ceasefire.”
Hamas blamed both Israel and the US-backed Board of Peace for the ongoing attacks. The group said the board “bears political and moral responsibility for the continuation of these crimes as a result of its silence and failure to halt the aggression, and its continued provision of cover and support to the occupation.”
The board was established by the Trump administration and backed by a UN Security Council resolution to advance the Gaza ceasefire plan signed in October 2025. But the plan stalled within weeks of its implementation, and much of Gaza remains in ruins.
On Tuesday, Netanyahu spoke by phone with Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, who played a crucial role in crafting the ceasefire deal, according to an Israeli source who said they discussed Gaza.
According to Axios , Kushner urged Netanyahu to carry out Israel’s obligations under the ceasefire plan, which would require Israel to stop striking Gaza and begin withdrawing forces that occupy more than half of the enclave’s territory.
But Netanyahu has refused to make progress on the 20-point plan until Hamas is completely disarmed. Last week, Defense Minister Israel Katz said that Israel “will not withdraw from the current lines of the security zones” until Hamas is “dismantled.” He also warned that Israel is ready to occupy more of Gaza.
Hamas has refused to unilaterally disarm, saying that it would only do so alongside a staged Israeli withdrawal from Gaza
Trump’s Board of Peace chides Israel for ‘insufficient’ response to Gaza flooding
In an extensive interview with New York magazine , Kushner warned that Israel was increasingly becoming globally isolated. “I feel like the fork in the road is Israel could rise from the tragedy of October 7, (and) be much more secure and much more integrated in the world, or they can go on the current trajectory, which is to trend toward global pariah status,” he said.
In another interview, with Mathias Döpfner , CEO of POLITICO’s parent company Axel Springer, Kushner called Netanyahu someone who “doesn’t always make it easy” to make progress in the Trump administration’s Gaza plan, and delivered his sharpest rebuke of Israel’s broader posture, arguing it should drop its “constant wartime mindset” and embrace economic diplomacy like Gulf Arab states do.
But Netanyahu has not shown any willingness to make concessions toward Gaza to advance the ceasefire agreement, particularly as his far-right allies have advocated for more strikes in Gaza and Palestinian emigration from the shattered territory.
On Wednesday, Kushner said in a podcast interview that Israel “needs to get out of the constant wartime mindset and focus on economic diplomacy.”
CNN’s Tal Shalev contributed to this article.

articles.title_orig: Bank of England sees growing financial risks as AI borrowing surges
articles.title_zh: Bank of England sees growing financial risks as AI borrowing surges
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By David Milliken and Phoebe Seers
LONDON, Nov 26 (Reuters) - The Bank of England said on Thursday that risks in the global financial system had intensified in recent months as the conflict in the Middle East dragged on, pushing up inflation and interest ‌rates against a backdrop of heavy borrowing by AI companies and governments.
Despite recent sharp falls in share prices due to concerns ‌about AI companies' prospects, share valuations still looked "stretched" and very dependent on them delivering the profits expected from AI, the BoE said in its half-yearly Financial Stability Report.
Complex borrowing structures to ​finance the expansion of AI and data centres remained a worry too, the BoE said.
"The very rapid expansion and broadening of its financing - in a form that is increasingly complex, circular and opaque - is... making it increasingly likely for stress in one area to propagate to another," the BoE said.
So-called hyperscalers building AI data centres were on course to issue more than $305 billion of debt this year, and broader debt issuance by the sector exceeded the annual borrowing of ‌most governments, including Britain's, the BoE said.
The growing ⁠global dangers were not a barrier, however, to the BoE setting out plans on Thursday to reduce the capital requirements of more domestically focused British lenders.
Ensuring that Britain's financial system would remain resilient if investor sentiment soured towards AI ⁠was a top priority for the BoE, Deputy Governor Katharine Braddick told a press conference.
"It's a very live part of our supervision," she said.
Governor Andrew Bailey declined to be drawn on whether turmoil at the top of chipmaker Nvidia reflected broader weaknesses in US corporate governance that could trigger financial risks.
But he noted the closer ​scrutiny ​that senior financial executives' conduct faced from regulators in Britain.
"I think the UK has ​made good choices in that respect," he said.
CYBER RISKS ‌REMAIN AT TOP OF BOE'S CONCERNS
The BoE also flagged risks from frontier AI models and – in the longer term – quantum computers capable of breaking existing widely used encryption techniques.
"The immediate financial stability priority is an orderly transition to quantum-resistant cryptography," it said.
Bailey added that there needed to be greater international cooperation – especially involving China – to test new AI models before and after their release.
"AI does not stop at the borders, and so we need to tackle these questions together," he said.
Current guidance calls for banks to migrate high-priority systems to quantum-resistant cryptography by the end of 2031 and all remaining systems ‌by the end of 2035. The BoE said firms with the greatest systemic importance ​should aim to move ahead of those deadlines.
Recent outages from Microsoft and Google's cloud services ​also showed the need for financial institutions to avoid being reliant ​on a single provider of critical software, the BoE added.
The BoE raised interest rates for the first time in ‌more than three years last month and financial markets price ​in an 80% chance of a further ​increase next month, followed by two more rises in 2027 when the BoE expects inflation to near 5%.
The BoE said 6.5 million British households were likely to face higher mortgage payments over the next three years, with a median increase of £100 ($131) a month - less than ​they experienced in 2023 and 2024, when rates last ‌rose sharply.
However, just over a million households who refinanced before rates last rose in 2022 face a median £200 increase in the ​next year.
Overall, the BoE judged British households' finances remained resilient with debt levels and servicing costs below their levels before ​the last financial crisis.
(Reporting by David Milliken; Editing by Toby Chopra)

articles.title_orig: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to purchase GPUs, sources say
articles.title_zh: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to purchase GPUs, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Neoclouds are being told they won't be able to purchase Nvidia chips if any of the computing capacity will be rented by Chinese companies, sources told CNBC.
It comes after a new rule restricting remote access to artificial-intelligence semiconductors was announced by the Trump administration on Nov. 16.
Chip sellers communicated the messaging to neoclouds after the announcement, which seeks to close an export controls loophole allowing Chinese companies to rent access to Nvidia's most advanced chips when hosted in data centers overseas, two people familiar with the situation told CNBC. The people asked not to be named when discussing private information.
The interim final rule was announced by the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, and came into effect on Nov. 19. Previously imposed export controls have effectively banned the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese companies and their import into China.
Prior to the new rule's announcement, Nvidia had said it would not sell its chips to customers renting more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, CNBC reported.
The new rule impacts the full supply chain, from the companies selling Nvidia chips to the neoclouds who rent access to computing power. Neocloud stocks have come under renewed pressure lately as investors questioned the sustainability of the AI boom.
Nvidia and the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The change has prompted Nvidia chip sellers to look for new buyers of the semiconductor giant's GPUs, CNBC reported on Wednesday, citing three people familiar with the matter. Two of those people said it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload GPUs because they were originally for use in data centers through which Chinese companies would rent access.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that the new BIS rule was intended to close "loopholes."
"Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries," he said.
U.S. lawmakers have been looking to clamp down on China's access to advanced compute.
Separately, Nvidia warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action," sources previously told CNBC.
